claim: The importance of an error in a scientific paper is determined primarily by its relationship to the paper's main scientific claims.
source_excerpt: The criticality of an error in a scientific paper is a function of its connection to the paper's core claims.

claim: Using two different state-of-the-art LLMs to generate errors is a sufficient method to prevent the benchmark from being biased towards the characteristics of a single model.
source_excerpt: This will mitigate model-specific biases in error generation.

claim: Selecting papers that were first published after the evaluation models' knowledge cutoff dates is a reliable way to ensure the models have not been trained on the test data.
source_excerpt: ensuring they were first posted on arXiv after the knowledge cutoff dates of the models we plan to test.

claim: Placing limits on the number and length of the text excerpts a model can return is an effective way to stop models from using simplistic, non-analytical strategies to solve the task.
source_excerpt: We will impose constraints on the maximum number and length of excerpts to prevent trivial solutions.

claim: The proposed automated evaluation metric will produce results that are consistent with the judgments of human experts on the same task.
source_excerpt: We will then compare the results of our automated evaluation metric against the human consensus to confirm its alignment with human judgment.
